item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves FilesService.Add behavior and adds the required validated, replayable Upload API using multipartbody.NewFile. Its main defect is duplicating Add’s request path instead of calling Add directly.","reasons":["A explicitly changes Add to eagerly buffer every custom multipart body, violating the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and potentially imposing new memory and reader-error semantics on lower-level callers.","B explicitly validates empty filenames and nil content before encoding, while A relies implicitly on multipartbody.NewFile and adds no visible validation coverage.","Both reuse multipartbody.NewFile and produce replayable Upload bodies, but A’s os.File retry test more convincingly covers streamed content than B’s strings.Reader test.","B violates the requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add: it duplicates option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data errors. This is a localized, straightforward correction—replace the duplicated request block with a call to Add—whereas A’s public Add behavior must be restored and its supporting test/changelog claims removed or revised."],"risks_a":["Changes the established lower-level Add API’s behavior by reading the entire body before request construction.","Adds memory buffering to all custom Add payloads, beyond the contract’s permission to buffer Upload content.","Upload calls a new private add helper rather than the existing FilesService.Add method exactly as required by the contract spirit and wording alike (while mutating Add semantics). A also lacks visible validation and source-reader-error tests."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add’s option, request, response-decoding, and error logic instead of routing through Add, creating maintenance drift.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader, already a replayable reader, so it does not strongly demonstrate that a streamed/non-replayable source is made retryable by multipartbody.NewFile.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, despite explicit contract coverage requirements."]}
